Read before drawing:
  > - G (154 models): S6+P5 is best or tied for k <= 12. At k = 32, ridge on the revealed benchmarks (S6+P2) beats S6+P5 by 0.29 [0.20, 0.39] points (helps at delta_T, matches at delta_floor); at k = 5, P5 beats P2 by 0.47 and P4 by 2.0. So P5 is not uniformly best; the inference claim has to be "best at small k".
  > - S7 (interview) is worse than random-k from k = 12 on G (-0.25 [-0.38, -0.12]); S3 (wrapper) from k = 20; S5 is behind S6 at every k; S6s equals S6.
  > - T (13 models) and S (22): small samples, wide CIs; P6 and P2 are lower than P5 at k = 12-32 on S, P5 on T k = 5. I would show G only in the main table and state T/S in the appendix.
  > - Not computable as a column: none in this file is a stand-in; the random-k spread is `rmse_sd_splits` (over C/T splits).

Please draw `tab3_pipelines.tex` (label `tab:pipelines` is what the text will use); I will place it in the appendix (Further results) unless it fits the main text.
  > 
  > What it must show: for the headline subset G (154 models, 51 organisations; these files use 20 of the 50 shared C/T splits, say so in the caption), selection S6 with inference P0-P6 (P0 has no k dependence), k in {1,2,3,5,8,12,20,32}: RMSE in points, and the paired difference to P5 (`diff_vs_P5`, positive = the rule is better than P5) with its 90% group-bootstrap interval and the verdict at delta_floor (`verdict_vs_P5_floor`; delta_floor is 1.15 points in these files). The S0 block (same columns) may go below or be dropped if width forces it; I would keep S6 only. Name the rules in the caption: P0 benchmark mean, P1 mean of revealed standardised scores, P2 ridge on the revealed benchmarks (trained on the EM-completed matrix), P3 kNN over training models, P4 Soft-Impute row update, P5 factor model (ours), P6 principal-component regression with a sigmoid link (an adaptation, not as published).
  > 
  > Reading I will state in the text (tell me if the table contradicts it): at S6 no rule beats P5 by more than delta_floor at any k (largest: P3 +1.04 [0.50, 1.57] at k=1); P3 is better at k<=2 and worse from k=5; P2 is better by 0.15-0.29 at k=20-32 and worse at small k; P1 and P4 are worse; P6 is within 0.32.
